caption:
Stanford physicists (Safavi-Naeini lab) watched single phonons, the quantum packets of vibration, jump between energy levels in a mechanical resonator in real time. Published in Science, 2026. Device details come from press coverage and are not yet checked against the paper.

#physics #quantum #science #stanford
voiceover_script: Sound does not fade away smoothly. At the smallest scale, it jumps. Sound is vibration, and vibration is energy. At the quantum level that energy comes in packets called phonons. A phonon can only sit on fixed energy steps, never in between. Physicists at Stanford, in the Safavi-Naeini lab, built a tiny mechanical resonator and watched single phonons jump between those steps in real time. It is the first real-time observation of a quantum jump in sound. The result is in the journal Science this month. One note. We have not checked the device details against the paper yet, so treat the specifics as reported. Source in the caption.
